questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The career of a powerful Hollywood film producer
The MeToo movement and the deeper causes of abuse
How hashtags spread so quickly on social media
Famous actresses who became political activists
questions.why: They discuss the MeToo movement against sexual violence and Tarana Burke's view of its wider causes.

questions.q: What caused the MeToo hashtag to become a global movement in 2017?
options: A new law passed by the American government
A TV documentary about abuse in the workplace
Serious allegations against a Hollywood producer
A famous speech given by Tarana Burke on TV
questions.why: Georgina says it happened when allegations against a Hollywood movie producer made headlines in 2017.

questions.q: What kind of women did Tarana Burke work with?
options: Marginalised women in neglected communities
Famous actresses working in Hollywood films
Women working in big companies and banks
Female politicians and government officials
questions.why: Georgina says she worked with marginalised women in neglected American communities.

questions.q: What word does Tarana Burke prefer to 'victims'?
options: Activists
Witnesses
Heroes
Survivors
questions.why: Sam says she doesn't call them victims but prefers the term survivors.

questions.q: What point does Tarana make about the women who came forward?
options: They were much braver than ordinary women
They were no different from the girls she'd helped
They were mostly from rich and powerful families
They should not have gone to the media at all
questions.why: She says they were 'really no different than those girls' she served ten years before.

questions.q: Why does Tarana call MeToo a 'unifier'?
options: It brings together actresses and producers
It unites different political parties
It brings together women of different backgrounds
It joins different social media sites
questions.why: Sam says it unites women of different race and social background, and survivors find community.

questions.q: According to Tarana, what allowed abusers like Weinstein to thrive?
options: Structures of power, privilege and love of money
The weakness and silence of individual women
Bad luck and poor timing in the film industry
The lack of social media before 2006
questions.why: She says it's about capitalism, the love of money, power and privilege.

questions.q: What does Tarana believe the MeToo movement has done?
options: Solved the problem of sexual violence
Ended male-dominated social structures
Focused only on Hollywood
Opened a new way to talk about sexual violence
questions.why: Georgina says Tarana believes it opened up a space to talk about sexual violence in a new way.
